anomalies.observed: The AVR-ISP-6 header J7 pin 3 (SCK) is on net NET0002, which connects only to J3 pin 4 (FAN). The ATtiny45 U3 pin 7 (PB2/SCK) and ATtiny13 U4 pin 7 (PB2/SCK) are on net NET0003, which connects to J1 pin 2 (POT) and J4 pin 3 (I2C SCL). There is no connection between NET0002 and NET0003.
anomalies.expected: J7 pin 3 (SCK) should connect to U3 pin 7 and U4 pin 7 (PB2/SCK) so the ATtiny can be programmed via the ISP header. The fan connector pin 4 should not be connected to the ISP clock.

evidence.quote: J7 AVR-ISP-6: SCK NET0002; U3 ATtiny45-20P: PB2 pin7 NET0003; J3 FAN: pin4 NET0002

anomalies.impact: The ATtiny cannot be programmed through the ISP header because the programming clock is not connected to the MCU. Additionally, the fan connector pin 4 is driven by the ISP clock during programming, which is unintended.

anomalies.observed: The potentiometer wiper (J1 pin 2) is connected to net NET0003, which is also the I2C SCL line (J4 pin 3) and the MCU PB2/SCL pin (U3 pin 7, U4 pin 7).
anomalies.expected: The potentiometer wiper should connect to a dedicated ADC input, not shared with the I2C clock line. The I2C SCL should be separate from the pot to avoid loading the bus.

evidence.quote: J1 POT: pin2 NET0003; J4 I2C: pin3 NET0003; U3 ATtiny45-20P: PB2 pin7 NET0003

anomalies.impact: The potentiometer will load the I2C clock line, causing unreliable I2C communication. The I2C bus will also affect the potentiometer reading. If both are used simultaneously, the board will not function as intended.

anomalies.observed: The fan connector J3 pin 3 (tach) is on net NET0008, which is not connected to the MCU tach input circuit on net NET0005 (U3 pin 3 / PB4, U4 pin 3 / PB4, R8, R9, D2).
anomalies.expected: The fan tach output (J3 pin 3) should connect to the tach input circuit and to the MCU PB4 pin (NET0005) so fan speed can be monitored.

evidence.quote: J3 FAN: pin3 NET0008; U3 ATtiny45-20P: XTAL2/PB4 pin3 NET0005; R9 10K bottom NET0005; R8 1K top NET0005

anomalies.impact: The fan tach signal is not read by the MCU, so the controller cannot detect fan speed or fan failure. The tach input circuit on PB4 is left disconnected from the fan connector.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains multiple connectivity errors: the ISP SCK line is misrouted to the fan connector instead of the ATtiny, the potentiometer wiper is shorted to the I2C SCL line, and the fan tach signal is not connected to the MCU tach input. These would prevent programming, disrupt I2C, and disable fan speed monitoring.
